small_guidance: Fix the conv_transpose3d kernel correctness: the BLOCK_IC loop is missing — the kernel currently loads all IC channels at once via BLOCK_IC padded to next pow2, but tl.dot requires BLOCK_IC to be a compile-time constant matching the K dim, and the masking on ic may be silently wrong when IC isn't a power of two. Add an explicit reduction loop over ic tiles (e.g. BLOCK_IC=16 fixed), accumulating tl.dot(w_tile, x_tile) per tile. Also verify weight layout: PyTorch ConvTranspose3d weight is [IC, OC, KD, KH, KW], so w_off indexing looks correct, but double-check the dot operand orientation (w_tile is [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC], x_tile is [BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_SPATIAL], so dot gives [BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SPATIAL] — that matches). The likely bug is that batch_norm running stats differ between fp32 reference and the custom path, or the mean-subtraction kernel reads bn_out before BN finishes; ensure bn_out is contiguous. Add num_warps/num_stages to the meansub kernel via autotune.
large_guidance: Redesign with a cleaner scatter-add ConvTranspose3d: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), scattering input*weight outer products into the output via atomic adds, OR keep the gather form but fuse BN folding (scale=gamma/sqrt(var+eps), shift=beta - mean*scale) into the conv epilogue so the BN call is eliminated. Then a second kernel computes per-(N,C) spatial mean and subtracts in a single two-pass persistent kernel. This removes the intermediate bn_out tensor and the separate BN launch. Use channels_last_3d layout so the OC reduction in the conv GEMM is contiguous. Verify correctness on a tiny shape (N=1, IC=2, OC=2, spatial=4^3) before scaling tiles.
